parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Define half-life of a radioactive isotope.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
Radioactive isotope X decays to isotope Y.

A sample contains only nuclei of X at time *t* = 0. Fig. 9.1 shows the variation with *t* of the numbers of nuclei of X and Y as the sample decays.

[[fig:f1]]
parts.text: State the name of the quantity represented by the magnitude of the gradient of line X in Fig. 9.1.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State three conclusions about X or Y that may be drawn from Fig. 9.1. The conclusions may be qualitative or quantitative. Use the space below for any working that you need.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The mass of radioactive isotope X in the sample in (b) is 7.3 × 10⁻⁴ kg at time *t* = 0.

Determine the nucleon number of isotope X.

figures.caption: Fig. 9.1
figures.alt: A graph of the numbers of nuclei of X and Y against time, with X decreasing and Y increasing.
